messages:
Samir Gupta: FYI tagging finance — Medivault (acct MV-998) disputed the Apr dedicated commit invoice. They say a partial outage on 2026-04-11 caused us to throttle their burst, and they're asking for a pro-forma commit reduction + SLA credit to offset overage charges. Invoice: INV-2026-0423-MV.
Dana Morris: Thanks. Did they send the usage breakdown? I can pull the telemetry but want to avoid duplicate work.
Samir Gupta: Attached CSV in their thread but summarized: committed tokens = 1,200,000; billed usage = 1,350,000; burst billed 150,000 tokens => overage charge ~$675 (rate $0.0045/1k tokens after commit). They want the overage waived because KB-cache missed during the outage.
invoice-bot: New invoice uploaded: INV-2026-0423-MV (total $7,150). Hosted at https://billing.redwood.internal/invoices/INV-2026-0423-MV
Raj Patel: Quick notes — per our Dedicated TOS, outages that drop throughput below SLA and are verified can trigger SLA credit but not automatic overage waiver. Credits apply to future invoices unless we approve a refund.
Alice Chen: Can ops confirm the outage window and impacted %? We need to compute pro-rata commit reduction vs SLA credit. If the outage reduced effective capacity by >20% for >30m, we generally offer a 10% SLA credit.
Dana Morris: Ops confirmed: 2026-04-11 03:42–04:10 UTC, 28 minutes, median node throughput down ~35% on their dedicated pool (pool-id ded-3c-7). They lost some prefix cache warmups; we saw elevated token retries.
Samir Gupta: Customer says that burst attempts during that 28m were rejected or queued so the effective billed tokens are misleading. They want us to: (A) apply SLA credit for outage (10%), AND (B) remove 75k tokens from billed usage as a pro-forma adjustment so net charge becomes ~ $375.
Raj Patel: Proposed calc here:
```
Committed = 1,200,000 tokens (monthly)
Billed usage = 1,350,000 tokens
Overage = 150,000 tokens @ $0.0045/1k = 150 * 0.0045 = $0.675? wait unit mismatch
Recompute: rate is $4.50 per 1M tokens -> $0.0045 per 1k tokens => overage charge = (150,000/1000)*0.0045 = 150*0.0045 = $0.675
Invoice total shown $7,150 includes base reserved fee and other items; overage small relative to base. SLA credit 10% of reserved fee portion -> approx $600.
```
Raj Patel: So SLA credit actually exceeds the overage amount. Policy: SLA credit reduces next invoice; we can apply a one-time invoice-level adjustment (credit now) if finance ops approves.
Alice Chen: Given the numbers, I'm leaning to approve a one-time invoice credit to avoid churn. Approve immediate invoice-level credit for the verified outage: apply SLA credit of $600 and an additional pro-forma adjustment to remove 75k tokens billed (equivalent ~ $0.34). Net credit ~ $600.34. Need manager sign-off.
Dana Morris: Customer success supports this — Medivault is mid-market, growing usage, risk of them pausing Dedicated if we push.
Samir Gupta: Requesting txn approval: refund vs credit? They want their card refunded for overage since they already paid. If ops apply invoice-level credit it can produce a negative balance; treasury prefers refunds < $1k to be issued rather than hold credits.
Alice Chen: I'll sign off on a refund for the $675 overage and SLA credit applied as a separate invoice-level credit $600 (net refund outcome $75). Finance to process refund and post the SLA credit as a memo.
Raj Patel: Noted. I'll create a billing adjustment ticket and tag treasury for refund: TR-REF-2026-176845. Dana/Samir — please do final confirmation with customer that refund + credit memo acceptable.
Samir Gupta: Will confirm with MV legal/POC now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
invoice-bot: Billing adjustment ticket created: ADJ-2026-6543 (linked INV-2026-0423-MV).
